root_cause: Pre-existing fork defect (f1b7aebff8c2). RISCVTargetLowering::allowsMisalignedMemoryAccesses answered 'allowed and fast' for the PULP packed types v2i16/v4i8 at element (2-/1-byte) alignment (upstream RVV element-alignment rule a5b07a221a57, plus the fork's '|| hasPULPExtV2()'). DAGCombiner::tryStoreMergeOfLoads therefore merged two adjacent i16 (four i8) load->store copies into one v2i16 (v4i8) load/store; LegalizeDAG promotes that to an unaligned i32 access, which the target does not support, and splits it back into i16 accesses; the combiner re-merges: infinite loop. Confirmed with llc -debug-only=isel,dagcombine,legalizedag. Not fp16-specific: plain short pair copies and 4 x char copies hang too (ref-18, port-20, integration head).
fix: One new block in allowsMisalignedMemoryAccesses: with Xpulpv2, v2i16/v4i8 get the i32 scalar answer (enableUnalignedScalarMem()), since they are loaded/stored as a promoted i32 lw/sw. The fork's '|| hasPULPExtV2()' line is kept (now only relevant for RVV types with V+Xpulpv2). Reference: scalar branch of the same function, RISCVISelLowering.cpp:21993-21997 at llvmorg-20.1.8; GAP9 GCC emits 2 x lh + 2 x sh for the same copy.
